answer: One concrete defense is slashable identity bonds. Every agent must lock collateral before it can trade. A random auditor then checks whether each new whisper of transactions comes from a distinct funded principal rather than a clone. To flood the harbor with fake peers, an attacker must post a fresh bond for every identity, so the cost grows linearly with the number of sybils. Any clones caught at the wharf forfeit their stake, making a majority attempt risk more capital than it could ever earn.
